title.narrative: Scaling Up Integrated Nutrition Services to Prevent and Treat Acute Malnutrition among Children Under Five and Pregnant and Lactating Women affected by drought in Tayeeglow District, Bakool Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtCurrently, GRRN in partnership with UNICEF provides nutrition services covering only 40% of the acute malnutrition burden/caseload. However, services remain fragmented and underfunded, leaving significant gaps in the provision of integrated health and nutrition interventions mainly in the rural villages. In addition, the projected situation in 2026 will worsen the situation with 25% increase burden expected. This proposal seeks to scale up nutrition services through two fixed health/nutrition sites, one Stabilization Centre (SC), and two mobile outreach teams, with a primary focus on vulnerable populations. The intervention will target 6,729 drought affected individuals, including minority and marginalized groups within the catchment areas, to prevent morbidity and mortality among children and women.ltbrgtThe intervention will also provide screening , management of facility-based and community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM). Routine screening and identification of children with acute malnutrition through a facility- and community-based approach. Severely malnourished cases without medical complications will be enrolled into the OTP program for treatment as well as Moderately malnourished children and PLWs. Children with SAM and medical complications will be referred to stabilization Centers (SCs). GRRN will adopt a comprehensive IYCF in Emergencies (IYCF-E) strategy, engaging not only mothers but also fathers, grandparents, community leaders, religious figures, and teachers to foster a supportive environment for improved child nutrition and GRRN practices. Mother support groups will be established and supported to promote IYCF sessions in the IDP camps. Consumption of locally available foods will be promoted through local available food demonstrations (kobciye), including the one egg a day approach. Capacity building will be prioritized through training of health workers on IMAM, IYCF, and inpatient management of SAM with complications, as well as training of community health workers (CHWs) and community members—including TBAs, Imams, and elders—on Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) and Community Case Management (CCM).ltbrgtWith a multi year Programme Document (PD) with UNICEF Nutrition Section, GRRN will scale up services with additional staff to screen and treat at least 70% of the SAM/MAM burden using the simplified protocol under expanded admission criteria. Furthermore, GRRN will sustain a stabilization center in Tayeeglow District dedicated to the treatment of children with SAM complications, ensuring timely access to life saving care.GRRN will develop a referral pathway for other partners in the area to ensure defaulters and missed opportunities are minimizedltbrgtlt/pgt
